sections.title: Executa — Anna's plugin extension system
sections.sub: An Executa is a standalone process Anna spawns and talks to over stdio. There is no SDK and no embedded runtime; any language that can read a line and print a line qualifies. Two declarative flavours ship today: Tool (executable JSON-RPC) and Skill (markdown recipe).

items.name: Tool
items.desc: A real process that runs and returns data. Long-running stdio JSON-RPC. Most common Executa shape.

items.name: Skill
items.desc: A folder of markdown loaded into the agent as a `@tool`. Skills do not execute code themselves — the agent does, via its built-in exec tools.

items.name: Single long-running process
items.desc: Anna spawns one process per plugin and reuses it for every `describe` / `invoke` / `health`. Plugins must loop on stdin until EOF — exiting after one request is the #1 pitfall.

items.name: Per-user spawn
items.desc: Each (user, plugin) gets its own process. Credentials are injected per spawn, never shared across users.

items.name: Stdout = data, stderr = logs
items.desc: Stdout is the JSON-RPC channel; anything written there must be a frame. Use stderr for diagnostics — captured into user-visible traces.

items.name: v1.0
items.desc: Forward request / response only. `describe` + `invoke` + `health`.

items.name: v2
items.desc: Adds the `initialize` handshake + reverse RPC channel (host → plugin requests). Unlocks sampling and persistent storage.

items.name: v2.1
items.desc: Adds agent sessions (`agent/complete`, `agent/session.*`) — parity with iframe anna-apps for multi-turn tool-using runs.

sections.title: Tool Executa — wire protocol
sections.sub:
**JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio**, one message per line (LF-delimited UTF-8 JSON, no Content-Length headers). Agent owns transport, request IDs, error wrapping, restart, credential injection and reverse-RPC routing; the plugin only has to read stdin and write stdout.

**Three rules that cause 90% of `Stopped` plugins:**
1. `stdout` is **protocol-only** — a single `print()` outside the JSON-RPC envelope corrupts the framing. All logs go to `stderr`.
2. **Flush after every write.** Most languages block-buffer stdout by default; pipe back-pressure plus no flush = silent hang.
3. **Never `exit()` after a single response.** The main loop must keep reading stdin until EOF, otherwise sampling/storage reverse-RPC has nothing to read host replies on.

Source of truth: the Anna Agent runtime (method names, error codes, limits, and spawn / restart / timeout policy).

items.name: stdin
items.desc: Agent writes one JSON-RPC request per line. Plugin must read line-by-line; handle empty lines as no-op.

items.name: stdout
items.desc: Protocol responses **only**. Any non-JSON-RPC byte breaks framing → host kills the plugin.

items.name: stderr
items.desc: Free-form logs. Captured and surfaced in execution traces. Never log credential values or `sampling_token`.

items.name: encoding
items.desc: UTF-8 everywhere. No BOM. No CRLF — LF only.

items.name: MAX_STDIO_MESSAGE_BYTES = 512 KiB
items.desc: Per-message soft cap. Larger responses MUST use file transport (see below) or risk pipe-buffer deadlock.

items.name: MAX_READLINE_BYTES = 2 MiB
items.desc: Hard line cap on the host's reader. A line longer than this is treated as a protocol violation.

items.name: initialize
items.desc: **v2 handshake.** Host sends `{protocolVersion: "2.0", host_capabilities: {"llm.sample": true}}`. Plugin must echo `protocolVersion` and advertise `client_capabilities` (e.g. `{sampling: {}}`). Plugins that return `-32601 Method not found` silently fall back to v1 (no reverse RPC).

items.name: describe
items.desc: Return the manifest (`name`, `version`, `tools[]`, `credentials[]`, `host_capabilities[]`, `runtime`). Called once per spawn and cached. **Result MUST be the manifest itself**, not wrapped — `from_dict` reads `data["name"]` directly.

items.name: invoke
items.desc: Execute one tool. Per-tool timeout defaults to **60s** and can be overridden via `ToolDefinition.timeout`. Streaming flag exists but invoke is request/response in v2 (streaming reserved for a future revision).

items.name: health
items.desc: Optional liveness probe. Return `{status: "healthy", timestamp, version, tools_count}`. Host uses it to decide restart timing and surface red dots in Admin.

items.name: shutdown
items.desc: Reserved graceful-shutdown method. In practice host closes stdin → SIGTERM → SIGKILL on a 5s grace window. Plugins should treat stdin EOF as the actual shutdown signal.

items.name: sampling/createMessage
items.desc: Borrow the host's LLM for a single completion. Requires v2 negotiation + manifest `host_capabilities: ["llm.sample"]` + user grant. See `executa-sampling`.

items.name: agent/session.create · run · cancel · history · delete
items.desc: Drive multi-turn stateful agent sessions from a plugin. Requires `host_capabilities: ["llm.agent.auto"]`. See `executa-agent-sessions`.

items.name: agent/complete
items.desc: L1 stateless single-turn completion (convenience wrapper, same auth chain as `agent/session.*`).

items.name: storage/get · set · delete · list
items.desc: Anna Persistent Storage KV. Scope selected via `scope: "user"|"app"|"tool"`; server-side gated by the `storage_token`'s `allowed_scopes` claim. See `executa-persistent-storage`.

items.name: files/upload_begin · upload_complete · download_url · list · delete
items.desc: Anna Persistent Storage Files namespace (covers all three scopes). The legacy `user_files/*` alias was removed in favour of `files/*` + `scope="user"`.

items.name: Reverse-RPC dispatch contract
items.desc: Plugin uses the **same stdin reader** for incoming forward requests AND for host responses to its own reverse RPCs. Use the SDK's `dispatch_response` helper — naive `readline()` loops will hang the moment sampling is in flight.

items.name: name
items.desc: Unique tool identifier. Lowercase kebab/snake-case. Maps to `tool_id` in Anna Admin.

items.name: display_name
items.desc: Human-readable name. Maps to `name` in Admin UI.

items.name: version
items.desc: Semantic version. Used for installed-vs-published diff and INSTALL.json bookkeeping.

items.name: description
items.desc: Plugin-level description shown in Anna Admin and the catalogue.

items.name: tools[]
items.desc: Array of `ToolDefinition`. Each item: `{name, description, parameters[], timeout?, streaming?}`. `description` is what the LLM sees — write for the model, not the developer.

items.name: credentials[]
items.desc: Array of `CredentialSchema`. Declares API keys / OAuth tokens the plugin needs; host renders config UI and injects via `context.credentials`. See `executa-credentials`.

items.name: host_capabilities[]
items.desc: Whitelist of reverse-RPC families this plugin intends to use: `"llm.sample"`, `"llm.agent.auto"`, `"storage"`, …. Missing entries → host rejects the corresponding reverse RPC with `not_negotiated` / `not_granted`.

items.name: runtime
items.desc: Optional `{type: "binary"|"uv"|"npm"|…, min_version?}` hint. Host uses it for compatibility checks; the actual runtime is decided by the distribution type (see `executa-distribution`).

items.name: author
items.desc: Optional. Displayed in catalogue. Not validated.

items.name: name
items.desc: Argument name as the LLM will pass it.

items.name: type
items.desc: One of `string` · `integer` · `number` · `boolean` · `array` · `object`. **Use the protocol's `parameters[]` shape, NOT MCP `input_schema`** — `input_schema` is silently ignored by `ToolDefinition.from_dict`.

items.name: description
items.desc: Shown to the LLM. Critical for argument quality.

items.name: required
items.desc: Default `true`. Set `false` for optional args.

items.name: default
items.desc: Optional. Used by the host when LLM omits the arg.

items.name: enum
items.desc: Optional list of allowed values; surfaced as a constrained JSON Schema enum.

items.name: items / items_type (array only)
items.desc: **Required when `type="array"`** or the LLM will serialise the array as a quoted string (`"['/path']"`). Two equivalent forms: `items: {type: "string"}` (standard JSON Schema) or `items_type: "string"` (shorthand). Missing → host defaults to `string` and warns.

items.name: params.tool
items.desc: Tool name (must match a `tools[].name` from describe).

items.name: params.arguments
items.desc: Object of validated args; populated by the LLM.

items.name: params.context.credentials
items.desc: Host-injected credentials keyed by `CredentialSchema.name`. Never visible to the LLM. Plugins should read these first and fall back to env vars only for local dev.

items.name: params.invoke_id (v2)
items.desc: Per-invoke correlation UUID. Plugin MUST echo it in every reverse-RPC `metadata` field — billing/audit attributes spend to this id.

items.name: params.sampling_token (v2)
items.desc: Short-lived JWT (TTL 600s). Only present when the user granted sampling for this Executa. Required to call `sampling/*` or `agent/*`.

items.name: result.success
items.desc: **Boolean, defaults to `false` in the parser** — you MUST set `true` explicitly on success or the host treats the call as failed.

items.name: result.data
items.desc: Tool-defined payload. Free-form JSON.

items.name: result.tool
items.desc: Echo of the tool name for log correlation. Recommended.

items.name: error envelope
items.desc: Use JSON-RPC `error: {code, message, data?}` for programmer/validation errors. Use `result: {success:false, error: "..."}` for user-facing tool failures the LLM should see and retry-or-route around.

items.name: -32700 Parse error
items.desc: Request body is not valid JSON. Host-emitted.

items.name: -32600 Invalid request
items.desc: Missing `jsonrpc` or `method`.

items.name: -32601 Method not found
items.desc: Unknown RPC method or unknown tool name. **Always return this for unknown methods** — the host's v1/v2 fallback depends on it.

items.name: -32602 Invalid params
items.desc: Missing required argument or type mismatch.

items.name: -32603 Internal error
items.desc: Plugin caught an exception during tool execution. Never crash the main loop — wrap exceptions and return this.

items.name: -32001 SAMPLING_NOT_GRANTED
items.desc: User has not enabled sampling grant for this Executa.

items.name: -32002 SAMPLING_QUOTA_EXCEEDED
items.desc: User account quota exhausted.

items.name: -32003 SAMPLING_PROVIDER_ERROR
items.desc: Upstream LLM provider failed.

items.name: -32004 SAMPLING_INVALID_REQUEST
items.desc: Malformed sampling params (e.g. `maxTokens` missing or > 8192).

items.name: -32005 SAMPLING_TIMEOUT
items.desc: Sampling exceeded host wall-clock budget (default 90s).

items.name: -32006 SAMPLING_MAX_CALLS_EXCEEDED
items.desc: Per-invoke call cap reached (default 8).

items.name: -32007 SAMPLING_MAX_TOKENS_EXCEEDED
items.desc: Per-invoke cumulative token cap reached (default 32k).

items.name: -32008 SAMPLING_NOT_NEGOTIATED
items.desc: Host didn't negotiate v2 OR manifest is missing `host_capabilities: ["llm.sample"]`.

items.name: -32009 SAMPLING_USER_DENIED
items.desc: User explicitly rejected this sampling request.

items.name: -32021 STORAGE_NOT_GRANTED
items.desc: Missing `storage_token` or requested scope not in `allowed_scopes`.

items.name: -32022 NOT_FOUND
items.desc: KV key or file does not exist.

items.name: -32023 PRECONDITION_FAILED
items.desc: `if_match` etag check failed or generation mismatch.

items.name: -32024 QUOTA_EXCEEDED
items.desc: User hit the 5 GB (or plan-specific) storage cap.

items.name: -32025 VALUE_TOO_LARGE
items.desc: Single value exceeds the KV per-entry limit.

items.name: -32026 RATE_LIMITED
items.desc: Throttled by Nexus.

items.name: -32027 INVALID_PATH
items.desc: Path violates the design §6.4 validation rules (traversal, reserved prefix, …).

items.name: -32028 INVALID_REQUEST
items.desc: Generic input validation failure.

items.name: -32029 UPSTREAM_ERROR
items.desc: Nexus 5xx or network failure.

items.name: -32041 AGENT_NOT_GRANTED
items.desc: User has not granted plugin → agent access (no `llm.agent.auto`).

items.name: -32042 SESSION_NOT_FOUND
items.desc: `app_session_uuid` not in host cache (likely a fresh process).

items.name: -32043 INVALID_REQUEST
items.desc: Malformed `agent/*` payload.

items.name: -32044 SUBMODE_MISMATCH
items.desc: User authorisation doesn't match requested `submode` / `fixed_client`.

items.name: -32045 QUOTA_EXCEEDED
items.desc: Hit user quota OR per-run 4 096-frame cap.

items.name: -32046 PROVIDER_ERROR
items.desc: Nexus / upstream LLM failure during the agent run.

items.name: -32047 RATE_LIMITED
items.desc: Throttled.

items.name: -32048 TOOL_NOT_GRANTED
items.desc: Tool requested is outside the user's authorised whitelist.

items.name: INITIALIZE_TIMEOUT = 5s
items.desc: v2 handshake. Plugin must answer (even with `Method not found`) within 5s.

items.name: DESCRIBE_TIMEOUT = 5s
items.desc: Normal manifest fetch.

items.name: DESCRIBE_TIMEOUT_BINARY_COLD_START = 60s
items.desc: First spawn of a `binary` distribution: PyInstaller-style onefile bundles need to unpack, mmap, possibly Rosetta-translate on Apple Silicon.

items.name: HEALTH_TIMEOUT = 3s
items.desc: Liveness probe.

items.name: DEFAULT_INVOKE_TIMEOUT = 60s
items.desc: Per-tool override via `ToolDefinition.timeout`.

items.name: DEFAULT_SAMPLING_TIMEOUT = 90s
items.desc: Extra 30s headroom over invoke to cover slow / thinking models.

items.name: MAX_RESTART_ATTEMPTS = 3
items.desc: Host restarts a crashed plugin up to 3 times with exponential backoff (`RESTART_BACKOFF_BASE = 1.0s`) before marking it Stopped.

items.name: When to use
items.desc: Any single response > 512 KiB. Otherwise the pipe buffer can deadlock both sides.

items.name: Pointer envelope
items.desc: Plugin writes the full JSON-RPC response to a temp file (same user, same machine, readable by host) and sends `{jsonrpc:"2.0", id, __file_transport: "/tmp/executa-resp-xxxx.json"}` on stdout.

items.name: Host behaviour
items.desc: Reads the file, deletes it, processes the contents as a normal response.

items.name: Must still flush
items.desc: The pointer line itself must be flushed — file transport only saves the **body** from going through the pipe.

items.name: stdout protocol only
items.desc: Any rogue `print()` / `console.log()` / `fmt.Println()` corrupts the JSON-RPC stream.

items.name: Flush after every write
items.desc: Python: `sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)` or `flush()` per write. Go: `bufio.Writer` + `Flush()`. Rust: `BufWriter::flush()`. Node: line-buffered by default.

items.name: describe result is bare
items.desc: Return the manifest dict directly. `_ok(id, {"manifest": …})` → `KeyError: 'name'`, plugin gets dropped.

items.name: invoke result is wrapped
items.desc: Return `{"success": true, "data": …, "tool": …}`. The parser defaults `success` to `false`, so omitting it silently fails.

items.name: parameters[] not input_schema
items.desc: MCP-style JSON-Schema is silently ignored — the LLM ends up hallucinating argument names.

items.name: Unknown method → -32601
items.desc: Never crash on unknown methods; the v1/v2 fallback relies on `Method not found`.

items.name: Never exit() after one response
items.desc: Main loop reads stdin until EOF. Exiting early breaks sampling/agent/storage reverse RPC.

items.name: Credentials never in tool schema
items.desc: Declare them via `credentials[]`; receive via `context.credentials`. They must be invisible to the LLM.

sections.title: Spawn → initialize → describe → invoke → shutdown
sections.sub: Five phases every Executa goes through. The `initialize` handshake is what negotiates v2 capabilities (sampling, storage); a plugin that returns `Method not found` silently downgrades to v1.

items.name: spawn
items.desc: Anna starts the process with the user's environment; stdin/stdout/stderr piped.

items.name: initialize
items.desc: v2 handshake. Plugin advertises capability set; host advertises reverse-RPC support. Skipping it = v1 mode.

items.name: describe
items.desc: Manifest fetch. Cached for the process's life. 60s on first launch of a binary onefile, 5s thereafter.

items.name: invoke (loop)
items.desc: Hot path. Each request can also unlock reverse-RPC frames (sampling/agent/storage) if v2 negotiated.

items.name: shutdown
items.desc: Host closes stdin → SIGTERM → SIGKILL. Plugin must keep reading stdin until EOF; never `exit()` after a single response.

sections.title: Sampling — borrow the host's LLM
sections.sub:
Let a long-running Executa plugin ask its host (Anna) to perform an LLM completion **on the user's behalf** — no API key, no model selection, no quota tracking in the plugin. Modelled on MCP `sampling/createMessage`.

**Pre-requisites** (all three required):
1. **v2 protocol negotiation.** The host's `initialize` advertises `protocolVersion: 2.0`; the plugin must respond with the same version and `client_capabilities.sampling = {}`.
2. **Manifest declaration.** `host_capabilities: ["llm.sample"]`. Missing this → `-32008 SAMPLING_NOT_NEGOTIATED`.
3. **User grant.** The user enables sampling for this Executa in Anna Admin (`UserExecuta.custom_config.sampling_grant.enabled = true`, with `maxCalls` and `maxTokensTotal` caps). Missing this → `-32001 SAMPLING_NOT_GRANTED`.

**Per-invoke caps (v1 limits):** `maxTokens` per call defaults to **8,192** (`DEFAULT_SAMPLING_MAX_TOKENS_PER_CALL`); calls per `invoke_id` cap at **8** (`DEFAULT_SAMPLING_MAX_CALLS_PER_INVOKE`); cumulative tokens per invoke cap at **32,000**; `sampling_token` TTL **600s**; only `includeContext: "none"` is supported in v1.

**Model selection precedence:** `modelPreferences.hints[*].name` (case-insensitive substring; cheapest wins when `costPriority > 0`) → user's saved `preferred_model` → default provider's cheapest active model. Plugins should normally omit `modelPreferences` so user-level preferences apply.

**Common pitfalls:** the same stdin reader receives both agent-initiated requests AND host responses to reverse RPCs (use the SDK's `dispatch_response` helper); never `exit()` after a single invoke (sampling is async); always echo `invoke_id` in `metadata` so Nexus can attribute spend.

items.name: sampling/createMessage
items.desc: Single-shot LLM completion on the user's behalf. No API key, no model picking, no metering — host routes to the user's chosen provider and bills their plan. Equivalent to MCP sampling.

sections.title: Agent sessions — multi-turn tool-using runs
sections.sub:
Drive **stateful, tool-using Anna Agent sessions** from a stdio Executa plugin through reverse JSON-RPC — the same surface area an in-iframe `anna-app` gets, with the same auth boundaries, the same tool-grant model, and the same wire frames. Builds on top of sampling: sampling is single-turn; agent sessions are stateful, support tool calls the host runs, emit streaming frames (`delta`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `final`), and support cancellation.

**Pre-requisites.** Manifest must declare **both** grants:
- `host_capabilities: ["llm.sample"]` — unlocks `sampling/*` and `agent/complete` (L1 single-turn).
- `host_capabilities: ["llm.agent.auto"]` — unlocks `agent/session.*` (L2 multi-turn). Missing this → `-32041 AGENT_NOT_GRANTED`.

**Auth chain.** The plugin **never holds a bearer token**. Matrix host owns the secret: the plugin sends `agent/session.create` carrying the per-invoke `sampling_token`; the host mints an `app_session_token` via Nexus `POST /copilot/app/sessions/from_sampling`, caches it keyed by `(user_id, hash(plugin_name))`, and attaches it to outbound HTTP for every `run|cancel|delete`. The token is never returned to the plugin.

**Plugin/anna-app symmetry.** A Python plugin and a TypeScript anna-app should be **drop-in interchangeable** for the same agent workload. The only difference is transport: anna-app uses a postMessage channel, plugin uses stdio JSON-RPC.

**v2 limitations.** `agent/session.run` is **buffered** — host accumulates SSE frames and returns once `done=true`. SDK API (`async for frame`) matches the future real-time path. Hard cap: **4,096 frames per run** → `-32045 QUOTA_EXCEEDED`. `agent/session.history` returns `[]` until a public GET endpoint lands.

items.name: agent/complete
items.desc: L1 one-shot completion via Anna server's `POST /copilot/app/complete`. Sugar for plugins that don't need state.

items.name: agent/session.create
items.desc: Open a stateful, tool-using agent session bound to the calling user. Identity (`user_id`, `executa_id`) is derived from the sampling_token — the plugin cannot override it.

items.name: agent/session.run
items.desc: Submit a turn; receive buffered SSE frames (`delta`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `final`). 4,096-frame cap per run.

items.name: agent/session.history
items.desc: Read prior turns of a session. Returns `[]` until the upstream GET endpoint lands.

items.name: agent/session.cancel
items.desc: Abort an in-flight `run_id` on the upstream session.

items.name: agent/session.delete
items.desc: Idempotent teardown; drops the cached `app_session_token` and tells Nexus to delete the session.

sections.title: Anna Persistent Storage (APS) — per-user KV + objects
sections.sub:
Give an Executa plugin a small, durable, **per-user** key/value + object store hosted by Anna — no cloud account, no DB of its own. Quota and access control are enforced by the host. After `initialize` succeeds, the plugin issues reverse JSON-RPC calls; each call carries the per-invoke `storage_token` minted by Matrix Agent.

**Pre-requisites** (all three required):
1. **v2 protocol negotiation.** Plugin advertises `client_capabilities.storage = {}` on `initialize`.
2. **Manifest declaration.** `host_capabilities: ["storage.user"]` (or `storage.app` / `storage.tool` for narrower scopes). Missing this → `-32008 not_negotiated`.
3. **User grant.** End user enables persistent storage for this Executa in Anna Admin (`UserExecuta.custom_config.storage_grant.scopes = ["user", ...]` with `quotaBytes` and `objectMaxBytes` overrides). Missing this → `-32021 STORAGE_NOT_GRANTED`.

**Scopes.** `user` — owned by the end user, visible across every plugin they grant. `app` — owned by the Anna App bundle, shared across all installs of that app for one user. `tool` — strictly local to (user × executa). Default to `tool` for transient state; ask for `user` only when the user clearly benefits from cross-tool reuse (e.g. saving a generated PDF into "My Files"). The `files/*` namespace covers all three scopes via the `scope` parameter; the legacy `user_files/*` alias family was removed.

**Best practices.** Prefer `tool` scope unless the data is genuinely user-owned. Keep KV values small — anything bigger than a few KB belongs in `files/upload_begin`. Always pass `if_match` on overwrite to avoid lost updates. Set TTLs on cache-shaped data. Encode metadata in the key (`notes/{noteId}`), not the value — keys are listable, embedded JSON fields are not. Always read back the `etag` from `storage/set` / `files/upload_complete` — never assume your client already knows it.

**Built-in user-storage tools.** For LangChain agents, Nexus auto-registers six high-level wrappers under the `user_storage_*` namespace (`user_storage_get` / `_set` / `_delete` / `_list` / `_files_save_text` / `_files_get_url`). The agent never sees the raw RPC; the tool wraps each call in a soft 5-write / 20-read per-invocation budget. Users may disable the built-in tools per-account via `UserSettings.disable_user_storage_tools`.

items.name: storage/get
items.desc: Read a single JSON value by `(scope, key)`.

items.name: storage/set
items.desc: Write a JSON value (≤ 64 KB by default). Supports `if_match` (optimistic ETag) and `ttl_seconds`. Quotas enforced by Nexus.

items.name: storage/delete
items.desc: Soft-delete a key (recoverable for 7 days).

items.name: storage/list
items.desc: List keys by prefix; cursor paging.

items.name: files/upload_begin
items.desc: Start a two-step object upload; returns a presigned PUT URL.

items.name: files/upload_complete
items.desc: Commit the upload after the PUT succeeds. Returns object id + etag.

items.name: files/download_url
items.desc: Mint a time-limited GET URL for an object.

items.name: files/list
items.desc: List objects by path prefix.

items.name: files/delete
items.desc: Soft-delete an object.

sections.title: Cloud Agent filesystem — what survives restarts, upgrades & reclamation
sections.sub:
Your Executa runs on an **Anna Agent** — either the user's own machine (local agent) or a managed Cloud Agent microVM. On a Cloud Agent the filesystem has **two tiers**: the root filesystem (ephemeral — rebuilt from the image on every upgrade) and a per-user **persistent volume mounted at `/data`** (survives restarts, suspend/resume and image upgrades).

**The official workspace contract is the `ANNA_WORKSPACE_DIR` environment variable**, injected into every Executa process. It points at the durable workspace root: `/data/workspace` on Cloud Agents, `~/anna-workspace` on local agents (users may reconfigure it). It is a real POSIX filesystem — directory trees, atomic write-then-rename, partial reads all work.

**Never hardcode `os.homedir()` / `~` as your workspace root.** On a Cloud Agent the home directory lives on the ephemeral rootfs and is silently wiped by every image upgrade. Resolve your root as `process.env.ANNA_WORKSPACE_DIR ?? path.join(os.homedir(), "anna-workspace")` (same idea in any language) and create an app-scoped subdirectory under it.

**Persistence is bounded, not eternal.** A Cloud Agent that stays completely idle is suspended (state fully retained), and after ~90 days of dormancy the instance **and its volume** are reclaimed. Treat the workspace as the durable *working set* — task state, intermediate artifacts, resume checkpoints — and persist *authoritative* results (finished documents, exports, anything the user must never lose) to **APS** (`storage/*` KV + `files/*` objects), which lives host-side and is fully decoupled from the agent instance lifecycle.

items.name: $ANNA_WORKSPACE_DIR
items.desc: Official durable workspace root, injected into every Executa process. `/data/workspace` on Cloud Agents (persistent volume), `~/anna-workspace` on local agents. Put all task/workspace files under an app-scoped subdirectory here.

items.name: ~ (home / rootfs)
items.desc: Ephemeral on Cloud Agents: rebuilt from the image on every upgrade or instance replacement. Fine for caches and temp files only — anything you cannot recompute does not belong here.

items.name: $EXECUTA_HOME / $EXECUTA_DATA
items.desc: Host-managed per-version install dir of your Executa (and its `data/` folder). Located under the persistent install root on Cloud Agents, but replaced on every version upgrade — do not store user data here.

items.name: APS (storage/* + files/*)
items.desc: Host-side per-user KV + object store (see the APS section above). Independent of any agent instance — survives instance destruction and reclamation. The only correct home for authoritative user data.

items.name: Agent process restart
items.desc: Same machine, same disks. Rootfs **and** `/data` both retained.

items.name: Idle suspend → wake
items.desc: After ~2 h without task activity the microVM is suspended (memory snapshot) and auto-woken on the next request. All filesystem state retained.

items.name: Image upgrade / instance rebuild
items.desc: The machine is replaced with a fresh rootfs from the new image. **Only `/data` survives.** Anything under `~` or other rootfs paths is gone.

items.name: Dormancy reclamation
items.desc: An instance left suspended for ~90 days is destroyed **together with its volume**. Workspace contents are unrecoverable afterwards; APS data is unaffected. Any later use of Anna resets the clock.

items.name: Volume capacity
items.desc: The persistent volume is small (3 GB by default) and has no snapshot/backup facility. Budget rendered artifacts and logs; ship a cleanup policy for finished tasks.

items.name: Working set vs authoritative state
items.desc: Workspace = resumable working set (task state, intermediate files, progress logs). At milestones — task completed, export produced — checkpoint the authoritative result to APS `files/*`. Per-change sync to object storage is unnecessary.

items.name: Atomic updates
items.desc: The workspace is a local POSIX filesystem on both agent types, so the standard write-temp-then-rename pattern gives you crash-safe updates. No special API needed.

items.name: Interruption recovery
items.desc: Persist enough state under `$ANNA_WORKSPACE_DIR` to resume after a process restart or suspend/wake. Do not rely on in-memory state across invokes — your process can be restarted at any time.

sections.title: Embeddings — borrow the host's embedding model
sections.sub:
Let a long-running Executa plugin ask its host (Anna) to compute dense embedding vectors **on the user's behalf** — no provider API key, no model name leaked to the plugin, no per-plugin billing. Sibling of `sampling/createMessage` but on an **independent billing surface** (`LLMRequestType.EXECUTA_EMBED`), so exhausting your chat quota does not block RAG / semantic-search workloads and vice-versa.

**Pre-requisites** (all four required):
1. **v2 protocol negotiation.** Plugin advertises `client_capabilities.embed = {}` on `initialize` (the existing `client_capabilities.sampling = {}` also works — the same `sampling_token` is reused for both surfaces). Missing → `-32507 EMBED_NOT_NEGOTIATED`.
2. **Manifest declaration.** `host_capabilities: ["llm.embed"]`. Missing → `-32501 EMBED_NOT_GRANTED`.
3. **User install / grant.** `UserExecuta.is_enabled = true`. Optional explicit opt-out via `UserExecuta.custom_config.embed_grant = {enabled: false}` → `-32508 EMBED_USER_DENIED`. Default when omitted: enabled.
4. **Platform switch.** `EMBED_API_ENABLED = true` (default). Setting to `false` shuts down both the plugin reverse-RPC path AND the iframe `llm.embed` path with `-32507`.

**Stable alias contract.** The plugin only sees host-stable aliases (`anna-managed-v1` → 1536-dim today). Real provider model name surfaces in `_meta.backendModel` for audit. Dimensions are **immutable per alias** — upgrades go to a new alias (`anna-managed-v2`), never an in-place dimension change. Persist `_meta.alias` + `_meta.dimensions` next to every stored vector so cross-version reads can refuse-or-reindex.

**Reject-not-truncate.** Batch > 64 items or any item > 32 000 chars fails the *whole* request with `-32504 EMBED_INVALID_REQUEST` — chunk client-side and keep an index map. Provider errors are flattened to a single `-32503 EMBED_PROVIDER_ERROR` (upstream status not preserved).

**Local-dev gotcha.** Both the python harness bridge (`anna-app-runtime-local` `SERVER_REQUEST_METHODS`) AND the Node `LlmBridge` (`anna-app-cli/src/harness/server.ts` `HOST_OUTBOUND_ROUTES`) must list `embeddings/create` → `(llm, embed)`. Either missing → `-32601 Method not found`.

items.name: embeddings/create
items.desc: Compute dense embedding vectors for one or many strings; returns OpenAI-shaped `{model, data:[{index,embedding}], usage, _meta}` where `model` is the host-stable alias and `_meta.dimensions` is the immutable per-alias dim.

items.name: host_capabilities
items.desc: Array including `"llm.embed"`. The Agent uses this to decide whether to mint a `sampling_token` carrying embed authority for the invoke.

items.name: client_capabilities.embed
items.desc: Empty object `{}` advertised on `initialize` for v2 negotiation. `client_capabilities.sampling` also works — same token.

groups.label: Common errors (full list in detail page)

items.name: EMBED_NOT_GRANTED (-32501)
items.desc: Missing sampling_token, UserExecuta row missing / disabled, or manifest does not declare `llm.embed`.

items.name: EMBED_INVALID_REQUEST (-32504)
items.desc: Empty / oversize batch, item > 32 KB, non-string input, unknown alias, or `executa_tool_id` / `tool_invoke_id` body disagree with the JWT claims.

items.name: EMBED_PROVIDER_ERROR (-32503)
items.desc: Provider timeout / rate-limit / 5xx, or non-object body. Upstream error code is NOT preserved.

items.name: EMBED_NOT_NEGOTIATED (-32507)
items.desc: Plugin disabled the client (e.g. v1 negotiated) OR platform-wide `EMBED_API_ENABLED=false`.

items.name: EMBED_USER_DENIED (-32508)
items.desc: User explicitly set `embed_grant.enabled=false` for this Executa.

sections.title: LLM image generation & editing
sections.sub:
Let an Executa plugin **ask the host's LLM stack to generate or edit images** — no provider key, no R2 credentials, no per-plugin billing. Anna routes to the user's preferred image provider (DALL·E 3 / SDXL / FLUX / …), bills the user's plan, stores the bytes on host R2, and hands the plugin short-lived HTTPS URLs.

**Pre-requisites** (all four required):
1. **v2 protocol negotiation.** Plugin advertises `client_capabilities.image = {}` on `initialize`.
2. **Manifest declaration.** `host_capabilities: ["llm.image"]` for `generate`; add `"llm.image.edit"` for `edit`. Missing → `IMAGE_NOT_GRANTED` (`-32101`) at first call.
3. **User grant.** End user enables image in Anna Admin (`UserExecuta.custom_config.image_grant = {generate: true, edit?: true, max_images_per_day: N, max_per_call: M, model_hints?: [...]}`).
4. **Active image-capable plan.** User must have ≥ 1 enabled image provider; otherwise → `NO_MODEL_AVAILABLE` (`-32109`).

**Three layered quota gates** (you must handle each distinctly):
- **Host hard cap** — `_MAX_N = 8` per call.
- **Per-call grant** — `max_per_call_generate` (default 4) / `max_per_call_edit` (default 1).
- **Per-invoke rolling cap** — `max_images` (default 4) tracked in Redis `img:invoke:{tool_invoke_id}` with 30-min TTL; shared across all `generate`+`edit` calls inside one `invoke_id`.

All three surface as `IMAGE_MAX_IMAGES_EXCEEDED` (`-32106`). Returned image URLs expire in ~30 min (`R2_TRANSIENT_PRESIGN_EXPIRY = 1800s`) — `GET` the bytes (or round-trip through `host/uploadFile`) for durable storage.

**Best practices.** Always inject `metadata.executa_invoke_id` so billing rows correlate. Set `timeout ≥ 60s` — cold-start providers (DALL·E 3, FLUX) often need 30–60s. Treat `IMAGE_ERR_PROVIDER_ERROR` with `data.subcall == "image"` as 'upstream timeout, do not retry immediately'. Prefer `image/edit` with a single `image_url` over `image/generate` with `reference_image_urls` when you have a source image — better fidelity, no inbound-fetch quota cost.

items.name: image/generate
items.desc: Generate N images from a text prompt; optional `size`, `reference_image_urls` (≤ 4), `model_preferences`. Returns transient host-stored HTTPS URLs.

items.name: image/edit
items.desc: Mutate an existing `image_url` per a text prompt; optional `mask_url` (provider-dependent). Returns new transient URLs — source image is not modified.

items.name: host_capabilities
items.desc: Array including `"llm.image"` (for generate) and/or `"llm.image.edit"` (for edit). The Agent uses these to decide whether to mint an `image_token` for the invoke.

items.name: client_capabilities.image
items.desc: Empty object `{}` advertised on `initialize` for v2 negotiation.

groups.label: Common errors (full list in detail page)

items.name: IMAGE_NOT_GRANTED (-32101)
items.desc: Missing grant, disabled executa, or manifest doesn't declare the capability.

items.name: IMAGE_MAX_IMAGES_EXCEEDED (-32106)
items.desc: Host hard-cap (8), per-call grant, or per-invoke rolling counter exhausted.

items.name: IMAGE_PROVIDER_ERROR (-32103)
items.desc: Provider 5xx / safety refusal / **upstream timeout** (`data.subcall == "image"`).

sections.title: Host-managed file upload
sections.sub:
Persist a binary blob to host storage **in the lifetime of one `tool_invoke_id`** without holding R2 credentials. Three modes share one wire method: **`inline`** (base64 round-trip, ≤ 8 MiB), **`negotiate`** (presigned PUT URL for direct R2 upload), **`confirm`** (register the post-PUT object and get a download URL). All return short-lived HTTPS GET URLs (~30 min TTL).

**When to choose this over `files/upload_begin`** (in `executa-persistent-storage`): use `host/uploadFile` for **invoke-scoped, transient** artefacts — image inputs to chain to `image/edit`, screenshots to hand back to the user, intermediate PDFs the LLM should re-fetch within the same turn. The objects are not enumerable, not user-visible in 'My Files', and TTL out of presigned URLs quickly. For durable per-user state, use `files/upload_begin` + `files/upload_complete` instead.

**Pre-requisites** (all four required):
1. **v2 protocol negotiation.** Plugin advertises `client_capabilities.upload = {}` on `initialize`.
2. **Manifest declaration.** `host_capabilities: ["host.upload"]`. Missing → `UPLOAD_NOT_GRANTED` (`-32201`).
3. **User grant.** `UserExecuta.custom_config.upload_grant = {enabled: true, max_files?: N, max_file_bytes?: B, max_total_bytes?: T, allowed_purposes?: [...]}`. Defaults: 16 files / 20 MiB per file / 80 MiB total per invoke.
4. **MIME denylist + purpose allowlist.** `purpose` ∈ `{image_input, image_reference, user_artifact}` (`host_upload_service.ALLOWED_PURPOSES`); MIME must pass the host hard denylist only (executables, `image/svg+xml`) — the per-token MIME allowlist was removed (forum #218), any non-blocked type is accepted.

**Per-invoke quotas are shared across all three modes.** Files counter increments on `inline` and `confirm` only (negotiate is free). Exceed → `UPLOAD_MAX_FILES_EXCEEDED` / `UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES_EXCEEDED`.

**Best practices.** Choose `inline` whenever payload is already in memory and ≤ 8 MiB — one round-trip vs three. Use `negotiate`+`confirm` for streaming or large payloads. Always store the returned `r2_key`, not the `download_url` — URLs expire, keys are forever (for the storage lifetime). Catch `UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE` in the SDK pre-check and gracefully fall back to `negotiate`. **Error code numbering diverges** between the Agent-side SDK (`-3220x`) and the Nexus gate; always match on `error_name` strings.

groups.label: Modes (one wire method, three SDK entry points)

items.name: host/uploadFile · inline
items.desc: ≤ 8 MiB base64 round-trip; one network hop; SDK pre-checks size cap.

items.name: host/uploadFile · negotiate
items.desc: Get a presigned R2 PUT URL (5-min TTL); plugin uploads bytes directly to R2.

items.name: host/uploadFile · confirm
items.desc: Register the post-PUT object; HEADs R2 to verify; returns transient download URL.

items.name: host_capabilities
items.desc: Array including `"host.upload"`. Without it the Agent refuses to mint an `upload_token`.

items.name: client_capabilities.upload
items.desc: Empty object `{}` advertised on `initialize` for v2 negotiation.

groups.label: Common errors (full list in detail page)

items.name: UPLOAD_NOT_GRANTED (-32201)
items.desc: Missing grant, disabled executa, or manifest doesn't declare `host.upload`.

items.name: UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE (-32204)
items.desc: Inline payload > 8 MiB, or `size_bytes` / actual PUT bytes > `max_file_bytes`.

items.name: UPLOAD_MIME_REJECTED (-32205)
items.desc: MIME malformed or on the host hard denylist (executables, `image/svg+xml`) — the per-token allowlist was removed.

items.name: UPLOAD_MAX_FILES_EXCEEDED (-32211)
items.desc: Per-invoke files counter exhausted (charged on inline + confirm, NOT on negotiate).

items.name: UPLOAD_NOT_FOUND (-32212)
items.desc: `confirm` called for an `r2_key` that has no object — the PUT failed or was never made.

sections.title: Credentials & platform authorization
sections.sub:
Plugins declare the secrets they need in their manifest. Users connect a third-party service **once** in `/settings/authorizations`, and every Executa plugin that lists a matching credential name automatically receives the value at `invoke` time — no per-plugin OAuth flow.

Values live encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and are injected via `params.context.credentials` on the JSON-RPC `invoke` call, so the LLM never sees them in tool arguments or transcripts. Resolution is **platform broker → plugin-stored fallback**; plugins may further fall back to environment variables during local dev.

**Multi-account.** A user may connect **several accounts of the same provider** (e.g. work + personal Gmail). Exactly one account per provider is the **default** — that's what classic `context.credentials` injection resolves to, so single-account plugins keep working unchanged. Account-aware plugins additionally get the `credentials/*` **reverse-RPC surface**: `credentials/listAccounts` enumerates the user's accounts (metadata only), `credentials/getToken` exchanges a short-lived access token for any one of them. Auth mirrors the other reverse-RPC namespaces — the host mints a per-invoke `credentials_token` (aud=`executa-credentials`) whose `providers` claim covers exactly the OAuth providers your declared credential names map to; the plugin never holds a long-lived secret and `refresh_token` never crosses the channel.

First-class providers: **Google** and **X (Twitter)** via OAuth2 (auto-refresh); **GitHub**, **Notion**, **Slack** via API key. Adding a new provider is a single `_register(...)` entry in `src/services/credential_providers.py` — no schema changes.

items.name: credentials[].name
items.desc: Stable identifier (e.g. `GMAIL_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `WEATHER_API_KEY`). Align with a provider's `credential_mapping` key to receive automatic platform injection; reuse the same `name` across plugins so the user enters it once.

items.name: credentials[].display_name
items.desc: Label shown in the per-plugin settings UI when no platform provider matches.

items.name: credentials[].description
items.desc: Help text — recommended to link to where the user obtains the value (e.g. `GitHub → Settings → Developer Settings → Tokens`).

items.name: credentials[].required
items.desc: Whether the user must supply this before `invoke` is callable.

items.name: credentials[].sensitive
items.desc: Treat as secret — masked in the UI, never logged, stored AES-256-GCM encrypted.

items.name: credentials[].default
items.desc: Optional pre-filled value shown in the per-plugin settings UI. Only meaningful for non-sensitive options (e.g. `"metric"` for a units selector); ignored for `sensitive: true` fields.

items.name: params.context.credentials
items.desc: Plain-text `{name: value}` map injected on every `invoke` JSON-RPC call. Multi-account: OAuth values resolve to the user's **default account** for that provider. **Never declare credentials as tool parameters** — that exposes them to the LLM in arguments and transcripts.

items.name: params.context.credentials_token
items.desc: Per-invoke JWT (aud=`executa-credentials`, ~10 min TTL) unlocking the `credentials/*` reverse-RPC surface. Auto-attached whenever your manifest declares a credential name that maps to an **OAuth** provider (`GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN` → `google`, …) — no extra grant. Its `providers` claim whitelists exactly those provider ids; Nexus re-checks per request.

items.name: Local-dev fallback
items.desc: Plugins should read `credentials.get(NAME) or os.environ.get(NAME)` so they keep working when run outside Anna (CLI tests, CI).

items.name: Resolution priority
items.desc: 1. Platform broker (`user_platform_credentials` via `credential_mapping`, default account)  →  2. Plugin-stored credentials (per-plugin settings, encrypted in `UserExecuta.custom_config`). Plugin-stored values only fill names the broker did not resolve. Users connect providers at `/settings/authorizations`; the backing REST endpoints (`/api/v1/platform-credentials/*`) are an internal surface for the Anna UI and **not** part of the plugin contract — plugins receive resolved values via `context.credentials` and must never call these endpoints directly.

items.name: credentials/listAccounts
items.desc: Enumerate the user's authorized accounts for one provider: `{provider}` → `{accounts: [{account_id, email, label, is_default, status, scopes}]}`. **Metadata only — never returns tokens.** Exactly one account per provider has `is_default: true`; the user manages the list (add / disconnect / set default) at `/settings/authorizations`.

items.name: credentials/getToken
items.desc: Exchange a **short-lived access token** for one account: `{provider, account_id?}` → `{access_token, account_id, expires_at}`. Omit `account_id` for the default account. Rides the per-row refresh state machine — an expired-but-refreshable token is refreshed transparently before return; a dead credential (revoked / needs re-auth) fails with `CREDENTIALS_NOT_GRANTED`.

items.name: Auth chain (credentials_token)
items.desc: Plugin → Agent stdio JSON-RPC → `ExecutaCredentialsHandler` → Nexus `GET /api/v1/executa/credentials/accounts` / `POST …/token` with `Authorization: Bearer <credentials_token>` from `ctx`. Gating is your manifest's `credentials[]` declaration — names are mapped through `find_providers_for_credential` to OAuth provider ids at mint time. API-key providers (GitHub / Notion / Slack) have no account dimension and are not covered.

items.name: tools[].multi_account
items.desc: Declare `"multi_account": true` on a tool to have the platform inject an optional LLM-visible `account` argument ("Target account email or id; omit for default") into its args schema. The value arrives as a plain argument — pass it to `credentials/getToken` as `account_id` (resolve emails against `listAccounts` first).

items.name: executa_sdk.CredentialsClient
items.desc: Python SDK client: `await creds.list_accounts(provider="google")`, `await creds.get_token(provider="google", account_id=…)`. Register with `make_response_router(…)` like the other clients. See `examples/anna-app-credentials-demo` for a full HOST-API-vs-reverse-RPC walkthrough.

items.name: Error codes
items.desc: `-32061 CREDENTIALS_NOT_GRANTED` (token missing, provider not covered, unknown account, or credential needs re-auth) · `-32062 CREDENTIALS_INVALID_REQUEST` · `-32063 CREDENTIALS_UPSTREAM` · `-32064` SDK-local await timeout.

items.name: Google
items.desc: OAuth2 with `access_type=offline` + `prompt=consent select_account` — `select_account` forces the Google account chooser so users can connect **multiple Gmail accounts** side by side. Selectable scopes: Gmail (read / modify / compose / send), Calendar (read / events), Drive (file), Docs. YouTube scopes are not offered — Google forbids requesting them together with other API scopes like `drive.file`. Aliases: `GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `GMAIL_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_TOKEN`, `GOOGLE_DOCS_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `GOOGLE_SHEETS_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

items.name: X (Twitter)
items.desc: OAuth2 with PKCE, HTTP-Basic token auth, `offline.access` for refresh. 20 selectable scopes covering tweets, follows, likes, bookmarks, lists, blocks, mutes, DMs and Spaces. Aliases: `TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `X_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

items.name: GitHub
items.desc: API-key (`github_api` provider) — Personal Access Token, fine-grained recommended. Aliases: `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN`.

items.name: Notion
items.desc: API-key — Integration Token (Internal Integration Secret). Aliases: `NOTION_TOKEN`, `NOTION_API_KEY`.

items.name: Slack
items.desc: API-key — Bot User OAuth Token (`xoxb-…`). Aliases: `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, `SLACK_TOKEN`.

items.name: $access_token
items.desc: Special value in `credential_mapping`. Resolves to the live OAuth2 access token of the user's **default account**; expired tokens are auto-refreshed using the stored refresh token before injection. For a non-default account use `credentials/getToken` instead.

items.name: $refresh_token
items.desc: Reserved. **Never** exposed to plugins — the broker uses it internally to mint fresh access tokens.

items.name: "FIELD_NAME"
items.desc: Literal field name from the provider's `api_key_fields`. Maps the plugin-requested credential to the value the user entered for that field.

items.name: Encryption
items.desc: AES-256-GCM symmetric encryption. Key source order: `NEXUS_CREDENTIAL_KEY` env var → derived from `SECRET_KEY` → plaintext dev fallback (warns loudly).

items.name: LLM isolation
items.desc: Credentials are injected via `context.credentials`, never as tool arguments. The LLM cannot see, log, or leak the values.

items.name: Least privilege
items.desc: OAuth scopes are user-selected at connect time — e.g. granting Gmail read-only without `gmail.send`.

items.name: Auto-refresh
items.desc: Expired OAuth access tokens are refreshed transparently using the stored refresh token — per credential row, so each connected account refreshes independently. Plugins always see a valid token.

items.name: Revocation
items.desc: Disconnect (per account) calls the provider's revoke endpoint (Google, Twitter) where supported, then deletes the row. Disconnecting the default account promotes the earliest remaining account to default, so injection never dangles.

items.name: Multi-account red lines
items.desc: `credentials/listAccounts` returns metadata only; `credentials/getToken` returns short-lived access tokens per call (audit-friendly); `refresh_token` never crosses either channel — the platform keeps it.

items.name: Align names with `credential_mapping`
items.desc: Use canonical names (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `TWITTER_ACCESS_TOKEN`, …) so the platform broker auto-injects. Custom names like `MY_GITHUB_KEY` defeat the broker.

items.name: Never put secrets in tool parameters
items.desc: Declare them in `credentials[]`; read from `context.credentials` at invoke time. Tool parameters end up in the LLM transcript.

items.name: Mark sensitive as `sensitive: true`
items.desc: Causes UI masking and ensures the value never appears in logs / audit trails.

items.name: Provide acquisition hints in `description`
items.desc: Link to the third-party settings page (`GitHub → Settings → Developer Settings → Tokens`) so users self-serve without leaving the consent dialog.

items.name: Declare `multi_account: true` on per-account tools
items.desc: Any tool that operates on "an account" (send mail, read a calendar, …) should declare the flag and honour the injected `account` argument via `credentials/getToken` — otherwise users with multiple accounts can only ever reach their default one. Mask tokens before they can end up in tool output / chat transcripts.

sections.title: Distribution, install pipeline & lifecycle
sections.sub:
How Anna ships an Executa to an Agent host. Source-based runtimes (`uv` / `npm` / `pipx` / `homebrew`) defer to the package manager; **binary** distribution lets you ship a self-contained executable per `{os, arch}` with sha256 + size verification and atomic versioned installs.

The matrix Agent's `BinaryRuntime` (`src/executa/runtime.py`) is the source of truth for everything below — platform key format, archive formats, resolution order, install layout. The Hub admin UI just edits the data this code reads.

items.name: `uv`
items.desc: Python tools installed via `uv tool install <package>` — default for the Python examples (`text-tools`, `storage-notebook`, …).

items.name: `npm`
items.desc: Node tools installed via `npm install -g <package>`.

items.name: `pipx`
items.desc: Alternative Python install path when `uv` isn't available on the host.

items.name: `homebrew`
items.desc: macOS / Linux brew formula install.

items.name: `binary`
items.desc: Direct download of a pre-built executable per `{os, arch}`. Plugin contains no source code; works on hosts with no runtime installed. This is what the rest of the section documents.

items.name: `local`
items.desc: Development-mode install: consume an archive already staged on disk. Skips the download; reuses the same extract / layout pipeline as `binary`.

items.name: Canonical format
items.desc: `{system}-{machine}`, all lowercase. `system` from `platform.system().lower()` (`darwin` / `linux` / `windows`); `machine` from `platform.machine().lower()` with aliases collapsed (`amd64` → `x86_64`, `x64` → `x86_64`).

items.name: `darwin-arm64`
items.desc: macOS Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4).

items.name: `darwin-x86_64`
items.desc: macOS Intel.

items.name: `linux-x86_64`
items.desc: Linux x86_64 / AMD64.

items.name: `linux-aarch64`
items.desc: Linux ARM64 (Raspberry Pi 4/5, ARM servers).

items.name: `linux-armv7l`
items.desc: Linux ARMv7 (older Raspberry Pi).

items.name: `windows-x86_64`
items.desc: Windows x86_64.

items.name: `windows-arm64`
items.desc: Windows ARM64.

items.name: String value (shorthand)
items.desc: Map each platform key to a download URL: `{"darwin-arm64": "https://.../my-tool-darwin-arm64.tar.gz", "linux-x86_64": "..."}`. Sha256 and size are not verified in this form.

items.name: `BinaryAsset` object (full)
items.desc: Map each platform key to `{url, sha256?, size?, entrypoint?, format?}`. `sha256` and `size` are verified after download — any mismatch aborts the install. `entrypoint` overrides the in-archive `manifest.json` for this platform. `format` is one of `tar.gz` / `tgz` / `zip` / `raw`.

items.name: Resolution order
items.desc: When the Agent installs, `resolve_binary_asset()` tries: 1. **exact** match on the current `platform_key` · 2. **OS-prefix** match (any arch with the same OS) · 3. **wildcard** key `*`, `any`, or `universal` · 4. if the map has **exactly one entry**, return it. No match → install fails with `No binary available for platform '<key>'. Available: <list>`.

items.name: Archive format detection
items.desc: If `format` is absent, `infer_archive_format(url)` reads the URL suffix: `.tar.gz` / `.tgz` → tar+gzip · `.zip` → zip · anything else → `raw` (downloaded verbatim and `chmod +x`).

items.name: Canonical source of truth
items.desc: Bundle a `manifest.json` at the archive root. Its `name` field replaces the caller-supplied friendly name (so the `bin/` shim, `INSTALL.json`, and `list_plugins` agree with what `describe` returns at runtime). Path-traversal names (`/`, `\`, `.`, `..`) are rejected.

items.name: `runtime.binary.entrypoint` — string
items.desc: Single shared entry for every platform: `{"runtime":{"binary":{"entrypoint":"bin/my-tool"}}}`. Relative to the archive root.

items.name: `runtime.binary.entrypoint` — dict
items.desc: Per-platform entry: `{"default":"bin/x", "windows":"bin/x.exe", "darwin-arm64":"bin/x-arm64"}`. Lookup order: full `platform_key` → OS segment (`windows` / `darwin` / `linux`) → `default`.

items.name: Entrypoint precedence
items.desc: `BinaryAsset.entrypoint` (per-platform `binary_urls` override) → in-archive `manifest.runtime.binary.entrypoint` → heuristic search (single executable file under `bin/` or at the archive root).

items.name: 1. Resolve asset
items.desc: Call `get_platform_key()`, look it up in `binary_urls`. Fall back to OS-prefix / wildcard / single-entry per the resolution order above.

items.name: 2. Download with progress
items.desc: Stream to a temp file `/tmp/executa-{tool_id}-{rand}`. The streaming pipeline emits `progress` events (bytes_downloaded / bytes_total) on the NATS progress subject.

items.name: 3. Verify size + sha256
items.desc: If the asset declared `size`, the byte count must match. If it declared `sha256`, the lower-hex digest must match. Mismatch → install aborts; no files are committed.

items.name: 4. Extract to staging
items.desc: Unpack into `tools/{tool_id}/.staging-{rand}/`. Members with `..` or absolute paths are rejected by `_check_safe_member` (zip-slip defence).

items.name: 5. Resolve entrypoint
items.desc: Apply the precedence rules above. Entry must live under staging (no `..` escape) and be a regular file.

items.name: 6. Permissions + macOS unquarantine
items.desc: `_apply_permissions` walks the staged tree (entry + anything declared `executable` in the manifest gets `0o755`; rest stays as-is). On Darwin, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine` is applied **recursively** to the staged tree — unsigned binaries Just Work for local dev.

items.name: 7. Atomic version commit
items.desc: Rename staging → `tools/{tool_id}/v{version}/`. If the same version already exists, the old dir is moved aside (`.old-<rand>`) for rollback on failure.

items.name: 8. Swap `current` symlink + bin shim
items.desc: Re-point `tools/{tool_id}/current` to the new version dir, then refresh `bin/{name}` shim. Existing scripts that ran `~/.anna/executa/bin/{name}` keep working without changes.

items.name: 9. Write `INSTALL.json`
items.desc: Records `url`, `sha256`, `size`, `entrypoint`, install timestamp, source `binary_urls`. Used by `list_plugins` and for GC of stale versions (`EXECUTA_KEEP_VERSIONS`, default 1).

items.name: `ANNA_EXECUTA_HOME`
items.desc: Override the install root (absolute path). Used by tests, sandboxed dev environments, and per-user installs on shared hosts.

items.name: `tools/{tool_id}/v{version}/`
items.desc: Isolated install root per version. `tool_id` and `version` are slugified to a flat `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` segment (`sanitize_tool_id` / `sanitize_version`) — `@scope/pkg` → `_scope_pkg`, empty version → `unknown`.

items.name: `tools/{tool_id}/current`
items.desc: Symlink to the active version dir. Plugin loader resolves binaries via this link so swaps are atomic.

items.name: `bin/{name}`
items.desc: Back-compat shim (symlink or `.cmd` wrapper on Windows) → `tools/{tool_id}/current/{entrypoint}`. Lets old scripts that hard-code `~/.anna/executa/bin/{name}` keep working.

items.name: `EXECUTA_KEEP_VERSIONS`
items.desc: How many old versions to retain after an install (default `1`). GC runs at the end of the pipeline.

items.name: `EXECUTA_HOME` (runtime)
items.desc: Injected into every plugin subprocess as the absolute path of its own `tools/{tool_id}/current/`. Use it to locate side-by-side `lib/` / `data/` files without hard-coding the install root.

items.name: `EXECUTA_INSTALL_V2=0`
items.desc: Emergency fallback to the legacy single-file install path. Disables the multi-file pipeline, version dirs, and `current` symlink.

items.name: Shape
items.desc: `{package_name, distribution_type, version?, executable_name?, binary_urls?, tool_id?, name?}` — see `install_essentials/streaming.py::install_plugins_batch_streaming`. Concurrency is bounded by 3 by default; per-plugin failures never abort the batch.

items.name: `tool_id`
items.desc: Stable identifier minted by nexus. Decides the install dir (`tools/{tool_id}/...`). When omitted, the Agent derives a slug from `package_name` (or, for binary, from the package/URL-derived friendly name).

items.name: `executable_name`
items.desc: Friendly name for the `bin/{name}` shim and operator UI. Optional for `binary` (derived from the package/URL when omitted); **required** for `local` to avoid a shim named after the archive filename.

items.name: Draft
items.desc: Owner-only. Edit manifest, swap `binary_urls`, iterate freely. Not visible to other users.

items.name: Version freeze
items.desc: `POST /executas/my/{tools|skills}/{id}/versions` snapshots the row into an immutable ExecutaVersion. Existing installs keep working at their pinned version.

items.name: Visibility
items.desc: Per version: `private` (default), `unlisted` (link-only), `public` (Hub-discoverable). Public requires a paid subscription.

items.name: Local / internal distribution
items.desc: Agent runs `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine` recursively after extract, so ad-hoc signing (`codesign --force --sign - dist/my-tool`) or **no signing at all** is fine for local dev and trusted internal hosts.

items.name: Public distribution
items.desc: For external users, sign with a Developer ID and notarize: `codesign --options runtime --sign 'Developer ID Application: ...'` then `xcrun notarytool submit ... --wait`. The notarized binary passes Gatekeeper without relying on the quarantine workaround.

items.name: Stable tool names
items.desc: Renaming a tool after publish breaks every saved conversation that referenced it. The server-minted `tool_id` is the only runtime identity; the host no longer reads a self-reported manifest `name`.

items.name: LLM-readable descriptions
items.desc: The `description` field is the prompt the model uses to decide whether to call your tool. Write it for an LLM, not a human.

items.name: Typed parameters
items.desc: Arrays must declare `items`; otherwise the LLM passes JSON-encoded strings instead of real lists.

items.name: SemVer
items.desc: Versions must be SemVer. Old versions remain installable; new versions don't auto-upgrade existing installs.

items.name: No mutable archives
items.desc: An ExecutaVersion is supposed to be reproducible. Re-uploading a binary under the same `{tool_id, version, platform}` without bumping the version means a host that already installed it won't re-download — there is no auto-update path.

sections.title: Common pitfalls
sections.sub: If your plugin shows up as **Stopped** in the Anna UI or never appears at all, one of these is almost always the cause.

items.name: Process exits after one request
items.desc: The protocol is long-running — the Agent spawns one process per plugin and reuses it for every `describe` / `invoke` / `health` call. Returning from `main()` (or calling `sys.exit` / `process.exit` / `os.Exit`) after one response triggers a restart on every call; the UI card stays **Stopped** and every invocation pays a cold-start delay. Always loop on stdin until EOF — the Agent closes stdin to signal shutdown.

items.name: Sampling: process exits before reverse RPC completes
items.desc: Same lifetime rule applies to `sampling/createMessage`. Exiting right after returning the `invoke` result kills the stdin reader before the reverse-RPC response arrives — plugin logs `unmatched response id=…`, host times out. Use the single-reader-with-dispatch pattern from `sdk/{python,nodejs,go}`.

items.name: Quick local liveness check
items.desc: `./my-plugin <<< '{...describe...}' &` then `kill -0 $PID` after 2 s — if the PID is gone, the process is exiting after one request. The `python/build_binary.sh --test` script runs this automatically.

items.name: Banner / debug text on stdout
items.desc: Stdout is the JSON-RPC channel — only line-delimited JSON objects belong there. A startup `print("ready")` / `console.log` garbles framing; Agent logs `Failed to parse JSON-RPC frame` and `describe` times out. All human-readable output goes to **stderr** (`print(..., file=sys.stderr)`, `console.error`).

items.name: Blocking stdin reads with extra buffering
items.desc: Use line-buffered I/O (`-u` for Python, `setvbuf` for C, no `--harmony-readline` tricks for Node). Block-buffered stdin will deadlock the handshake.

items.name: Forgetting to flush stdout
items.desc: After writing each response also `sys.stdout.flush()` (Python) — the Agent reads line-by-line and won't see a buffered response.

items.name: Three names must be exactly equal
items.desc: The Anna `tool_id` (minted with the 🪪 button), the `name` field your binary returns from `describe`, and the `name` in the archive's root `manifest.json` must be identical strings. The UI joins user-installed tools to running plugins by exact match; mismatch puts your plugin under **Extra Agent Plugins** or shows duplicate **Stopped** / **Running** cards. `manifest.json.name` also becomes the launcher symlink `~/.anna/executa/bin/{name}`.

items.name: Use `display_name` for the human label
items.desc: Only `name` has to match — `display_name` is the pretty UI label (e.g. `"My Tool"`) and is free-form.

items.name: Always ship `manifest.json` at the archive root
items.desc: Without it the Agent walks a five-level entrypoint fallback (asset `entrypoint` → `bin/{name}` → only-or-first executable) and ZIP archives lose Unix permission bits — auxiliary scripts get `Permission denied`, the wrong binary gets picked, the launcher symlink falls back to a URL-derived generic name.

items.name: Declare `permissions` for every executable file
items.desc: ZIPs drop the +x bit. Set `runtime.binary.permissions["bin/foo"] = "0o755"` for every helper script alongside the entrypoint.

items.name: PyInstaller `--onefile` exceeds the 5 s describe timeout
items.desc: First launch extracts the bundle to a temp dir; a 200 MB+ bundle can take 10–30 s, especially under Rosetta / slow disks. The Agent uses `DESCRIBE_TIMEOUT_BINARY_COLD_START = 60` only during the post-install scan (see the platform source); normal calls hit `DESCRIBE_TIMEOUT = 5` and fail. Prefer `--onedir` shipped as a multi-file archive (no first-launch extract); otherwise shrink the bundle (`--exclude-module`, audit `--collect-all`).

items.name: Missing `host_capabilities: ["llm.sample"]` declaration
items.desc: Even after v2 capability negotiation, Nexus refuses `sampling/createMessage` unless the *published* manifest also lists `"llm.sample"` in `host_capabilities`. Host returns `{ code: -32008, message: "not_negotiated" }` (constant `SAMPLING_ERR_NOT_NEGOTIATED` in `src/services/executa_sampling_gate.py`); Agent log says `executa X did not declare host_capabilities['llm.sample']`. Add the field, republish, ask users to update.

items.name: `-32007 max_tokens_exceeded` on a single small call
items.desc: The cap is **cumulative across the same `invoke_id`**, not per-call (default 32 000 tokens; host max also 32 000 in v1, mirrored in the Sampling authorization UI's `maxTokensTotal` field). Send fewer / smaller sampling calls per tool invocation, or have the user raise `sampling_grant.maxTokensTotal` in Anna Admin.

items.name: Forgetting `initialize`
items.desc: If you want sampling / storage / agent sessions, you must respond to `initialize` with your v2 capability set. Missing handler = silent v1 downgrade and `sampling/*` calls return `not_negotiated`.

items.name: Manifest schema drift
items.desc: Run `anna-app validate` before publish. The upload path runs the same JSON Schema check and rejects ambiguous types — catching it locally avoids a publish-then-fail round trip.

sections.title: Skill — markdown that teaches the agent
sections.sub: A Skill is a folder containing `SKILL.md` (markdown with YAML frontmatter) plus any supporting files. At runtime the loader registers each skill as a LangChain `@tool`; when the LLM picks it, the tool returns the skill body and the agent uses its built-in exec tools to act on it.

items.name: title
items.desc: Short human label shown in the catalogue.

items.name: description
items.desc: One-sentence "when should I use this?" hint shown to the agent.

items.name: metadata.execution_mode
items.desc: Hint to the LLM about how to apply the recipe (e.g. prompt-only, shell, python). Advisory only.

items.name: metadata.dependencies
items.desc: Declared tools/binaries the recipe expects. Surfaced inside the loaded body.

items.name: body (markdown)
items.desc: The recipe itself. Loaded verbatim as the tool's return value when the agent invokes the skill.

items.name: supporting files
items.desc: Anything alongside `SKILL.md` is bundled with the version snapshot — templates, JSON examples, sub-prompts.

items.name: Discoverable skills directory
items.desc: The loader (`src/skills/loader.py`) walks a small ordered list of paths; drop your folder into the first one that exists, reload the agent, and the skill appears.

items.name: Reload loop
items.desc: Drop folder → reload → trigger → revise. No build step, no restart of the host.

items.name: Same pipeline as Tools
items.desc: A Skill is just an Executa with `executa_type="skill"`. Same wizard, same REST surface, same Hub draft/version/visibility flow as `executa-distribution`.

sections.title: Anna App manifest fields
sections.sub: Top-level keys on the App manifest (stored in `anna_app_versions.manifest`). Unknown keys are rejected.

items.name: schema
items.desc: Manifest schema version. Integer in [1, 2]. Defaults to 1.

items.name: required_executas
items.desc: Executas the App needs. Each entry: `{ tool_id, version?, min_version? }`. `version="latest"` auto-freezes at publish time.

items.name: optional_executas
items.desc: Executas the App can use if installed but does not require. Same shape as `required_executas`.

items.name: host_capabilities
items.desc: Strict allow-list of host-mediated capability strings (validated against `_ALLOWED_HOST_CAPABILITIES`): `aps.kv`, `aps.files`, `aps.scope.*`, `llm.sample`, `llm.complete`, `llm.embed`, `llm.agent.*`, `llm.image`, `web.*`, `host.upload`. Each bundled Executa must also declare its own `host_capabilities`; per-invoke tokens are gated on the Executa declaration + the user's grant.

items.name: tags

items.name: system_prompt_addendum
items.desc: Text injected into the system prompt when the App is active in a turn. Max 4000 chars.

items.name: user_message_prefix_template
items.desc: Optional template prepended to the user message when the App is #mentioned. Max 500 chars.

items.name: ui
items.desc: UI bundle section: declares bundle entry, views, host_api grants, CSP overrides. See "UI manifest".

items.name: dev
items.desc: Local-harness-only config (fixtures, mocks, seed_storage, user_id). Stripped by `anna-app publish`; ignored by production dispatcher.

sections.title: UI manifest — windows, views, grants
sections.sub: The `ui` block describes the iframe bundle, the windows it can open, and which Host API namespaces the bundle is allowed to call.

items.name: bundle.entry
items.desc: Bundle-relative path to the SPA entry HTML.

items.name: bundle.format
items.desc: Bundle layout. Defaults to `static-spa`.

items.name: bundle.external_origins
items.desc: Origins the iframe is allowed to load resources from (CSP-aware).

items.name: view.name

items.name: view.title

items.name: view.entry

sections.title: UI Host API grants
sections.sub: Declare which Host API methods your iframe bundle may call, per namespace. Tokens are method names (e.g. `set`, `list`); the dispatcher refuses ungranted calls.

items.name: host_api.storage
items.desc: Per-method grants for storage namespace (`get`, `set`, `list`, `delete`).

items.name: host_api.chat
items.desc: Grants for chat operations: `write_message`, `read_history`, `append_artifact`.

items.desc: Window control surface: `open_view`, `close`, `focus`, `set_title`, `resize`. NOTE: `window.*` is ALWAYS granted by the dispatcher ACL (`host_api_allows`) — declaring it is optional/documentary.

items.name: host_api.files

sections.title: Platform tools — the agent-session tool universe
sections.sub:
What can an App agent session actually call? Two distinct regimes, selected at `agent.session.create` time:

**Sandbox (default when `quotaCaps.inherit_host_tools` is false/absent for your grant).** The resolved surface is a pure intersection — `AppToolRegistry.public_set ∩ manifest.ui.host_api.agent.tools (→ user grant) ∩ quotaCaps.allowed_tools [∩ dev_safe on harness PAT sessions]`. Every built-in below is INDIVIDUALLY grantable — e.g. `allowed_tools: ["fs_read_file"]` yields a read-only-filesystem agent that cannot write or exec (forum #192). Host-kit tools (fs / exec / browser) execute on the session's platform-pinned agent client: `fixed` submode targets `fixed_client_id`, `auto` targets the user's default agent — the pinned `client_id` always overrides anything the model supplies, so an App can never aim side effects at an arbitrary machine. Any name outside the registry is **silently dropped** (no error); an empty result means a TEXT-ONLY agent — side-effect claims in its output would be hallucinated (the run emits a `NO_TOOLS_AVAILABLE` warning frame). Use `agent.session.catalog()` to see the registry universe and per-tool `blocked_by` diagnostics BEFORE creating a session. Per-run `allowed_tools` further narrows a sandbox session's surface for that run.

**Inherit (`quotaCaps.inherit_host_tools: true`, requires the user grant).** The session gets the SAME tool kit as the user's main copilot — the platform built-ins plus every Executa the user has installed. This surface is user-specific and dynamic (can be hundreds of tools ≈ 100K prompt tokens — slower + costlier runs); `granted_tools` echoes `["*"]`, and the per-run `run_meta` frame is the authoritative record. Per-run `allowed_tools` does NOT narrow inherit sessions — prefer a sandbox session with an explicit allowlist when you need a policy like read-but-never-write.

The sandbox registry below is drift-checked against `src/services/app_tool_registry.py` in CI — registering a tool without updating this section fails the build.

items.name: web_search
items.desc: Search the public web (or news) and return concise, provider-agnostic snippets. Same capability as the Host API `anna.web.search` — shared provider routing, `web_grant` gating, result cache and billing (an agent-side call books an `APP_WEB_SEARCH` ledger entry against the session), so the agent surface cannot bypass Host API quota.

items.name: sheet_read
items.desc: Read an Excel workbook (xlsx/xls) attachment as structured, typed data — workbook overview, then paginated rows with `{v, d, t}` cells (dates as ISO 8601) and stable A1 locators like `Sheet1!A2:D18`. Only accepts platform-issued attachment URLs (the `document_url` from the attachment list or an `upload_local_file` result). Truncation is always explicit: follow `truncated.next_call` to continue reading. Books an `APP_DOC_PARSE` floor-CU ledger entry per call.

items.desc: Read a DOCX / PPTX / PDF attachment as structured blocks with stable locators (`para:N` / `table:M` / `slide:N` / `page:N`) — use `mode: "outline"` first for large documents, then read content windows. Only accepts platform-issued attachment URLs. Truncation is always explicit via `truncated.next_call`. Books an `APP_DOC_PARSE` floor-CU ledger entry per call.

groups.label: Inherit host kit — additional tool families (inherit-only, user-specific)

items.name: fs_* / exec_* / browser_* / web_search
items.desc: The same host-kit built-ins as the sandbox registry above — an inherit session always carries ALL of them (per-run `allowed_tools` cannot narrow inherit). `web_search` is the ONLY server-side search surface — the legacy free `ddg_search` / `ddg_news_search` were removed platform-wide (capability fully covered by `web_search`: `topic: "news"`, free DDG provider fallback, unified cache / circuit-breaker / billing).

items.name: generate_image / edit_image / analyze_image / upload_local_file
items.desc: Multimodal built-ins. With a vision-capable model, images attached via `run({attachments})` or uploaded mid-run are presented to the model DIRECTLY — `analyze_image` is the fallback for non-vision models. Bound to the session's model configuration, therefore inherit-only today.

items.desc: Per-user APS key-value + object storage (get/set/list/delete/save_text/get_url). Wired through user-path middleware, therefore inherit-only today — sandbox sessions use the `storage.*` Host API instead.
